findings.reason: Confirmed (high). Example 4.1.1 (published p. 22) says 'The morphisms [S/G] → [S/H] correspond to S-homomorphisms G → H', and item /127 copies it. That is false for a general diamond S. Since BH classifies H-torsors, take S = Spd ℚ_p, G = 1 and H = ℤ/2: the unramified quadratic extension gives a nontrivial H-torsor, hence a map S = B1 → BH that is not 2-isomorphic to the one induced by the unique homomorphism 1 → H. The paper only uses maps induced by homomorphisms, so the applications stand. The fix, describing a general map by an H-torsor with a commuting G-action and recording a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (high). Theorem 4.3.8 (p. 32) is stated 'with p, q proper'. Example 4.3.10 (pp. 32–33) applies it with C′ = X′ = S after assuming only 'that X is proper over S', and item /059 keeps the arbitrary correspondence c: Y → X ×_S X. Properness of p: Y → S is then missing, and with it the induced endomorphism and the integral over Fix(c). The example is right: Y a countable disjoint union of S = Spd C with c₁ = c₂ the structure maps has Fix(c) = Y and trace section 1. That section lies in ∏Λ but not ⊕Λ, so the compact-support integral is undefined. The fix, adding properness of Y over S (automatic for Y = X) and a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (medium). Item /072 (the ECD §27 comparison: c_X^* fully faithful, compatible with f^* and Rf_!) is planned at AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L1 and L2. In the atlas, L1 constructs the scheme-to-v-sheaf functor and L2 extends scheme compact support. L3, 'Characteristic-p cohomological comparison', is the stage that proves 27.1–27.3 and full faithfulness. The fix, adding L3 to /072 and to route 2's imports, is right.

Confirmed (medium). The proof of Theorem 6.5.1 and §6.6 (pp. 68–69) use three Fargues–Scholze results. They are the construction of the parameter ('[FS21, Proposition I.9.1]'), its compatibility with parabolic induction ('[FS21, Theorem I.9.6.viii]'), and 'the commutation of Hecke operators with excursion operators', applied to every irreducible constituent of the Hecke-operator cohomology. No item states any of them. The extraction mentions I.9.6(viii) only inside a sourceIssue correction, and ES5 only in route 1's brief. The fix, separate items planned at ES5 and ES7:parabolic plus the Hecke/excursion interface, is right.

Confirmed (medium). Appendix C.2 (p. 76) defines 'a Langlands triple' (M, σ, ψ): a standard Levi, a ν-tempered irreducible σ, and ψ unramified with −ν(ψ) in the positive chamber. It states that every irreducible smooth π is j_P^G(σ⊗ψ) for an essentially unique triple, '[Dat05, Theorem 3.11]', and uses this to define I(π) and λ_π. Items /123–/124 use π = j_P^G(σ⊗ψ) and λ_π, but no item records the definition of ν-temperedness, the triple or Dat's classification; route 3's brief names them only in prose. The fix is right.

Confirmed (medium). The proof of Proposition 5.1.2 (p. 45) uses '[Tit79, 3.6.1]' to place the image in the building of a point fixed by a strongly regular g in the apartment of T. It then uses [BT84, 4.6.28] and [BT72, 7.4.10] to move into L^+N(T, G). Item /079 mentions only 'proof through the Bruhat–Tits building', and no item states the Tits fixed-point result. ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2's bounded-subgroup fixed-point statement is weaker. The fix, an item for the Tits result as a source addition to the building direction, with the other BT citations checked, is right.
